q: A developer wants Copilot to modify several files, run tests, inspect failures, and iterate until the implementation works.
explanation: Agent mode adds autonomous planning, tool use, and iteration.

q: A team needs a reusable security-review specialist with its own instructions and restricted toolset.
explanation: A custom agent defines a specialist persona, instructions, and tools.

q: Which TWO statements correctly describe subagents? Choose two.

q: A developer wants Copilot to work asynchronously in a GitHub-hosted environment and return a pull request.

q: A running agent has misunderstood a requirement halfway through its task.

choices.label: C

choices.label: D

q: A security scanner must run deterministically at a specific point in an agent workflow.

q: A team wants to distribute agents, skills, hooks, and MCP configuration as one reusable package.

q: A developer wants a specialist available across all their projects rather than committed to one repository.

q: The primary goal is to keep a large exploratory task from consuming the main agent's context.

q: Which TWO questions are most important when evaluating an MCP server? Choose two.

q: Copilot should search an external documentation service but never modify it.

q: A custom agent needs access to an external issue tracker only when that specialist runs.

q: A developer wants to permanently teach repository coding style.

choices.label: D

choices.label: C

q: A trusted MCP server exposes highly privileged tools.

choices.text: Trust eliminates the need for authorization

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use content exclusion as the only safety control

choices.label: D
choices.text: Still apply least privilege and approval controls
